newsitem.title: UK: Centrica, Dutch Elsta agree gas supply deal.
newsitem.headline: Centrica, Dutch Elsta agree gas supply deal.

text.p: Centrica plc on Tuesday said it had agreed to supply one billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas a year through the U.K.-Continent Interconnector pipeline to the Netherlands' Elsta cogeneration power plant.

Centrica, the supply arm of recently demerged former monopoly holder British Gas plc, will sell around 1 bcm to Inkoopcombinatie Elsta VOF over eight years through its subsidiary British Gas Trading, Centrica said in a statement.

It is the first agreement by Centrica to supply a major continental end user directly, rather than through a gas trading and transmission company. It is also the first export sale of U.K. gas to a power project.
Deliveries should start in October 1998 when the Interconnector, linking Bacton on Britain's east coast with Zeebrugge in Belgium, is due to open.

Gas will be drawn from Centrica's portfolio of U.K. continental shelf reserves and gas purchase contracts. Delivery will be made at Zeebrugge, and the buyers will be responsible for onward delivery through Belgium and south west Netherlands to Terneuzen.
The Elsta plant, where the gas will be consumed, is a 406 MegaWatt cogeneration plant on the site of the Dow Chemical Co's chemical complex in Terneuzen.
